issues.legal_issue: A claim arising in the winding up of a banking company may ordinarily be decided by a summary application, unless the court directs or applicable court rules require a suit.
material_facts: The bank was in liquidation when its liquidator sought the tenant’s ejectment for failure to vacate after notice terminating the tenancy.
The liquidator sought ejectment by application in the High Court, which granted an ex parte decree.
The relief sought fell within the scope of claims and questions arising in the winding up.
No specific statutory procedure or High Court rule requiring a suit was identified as applicable to the claim.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was competent to decide the ejectment claim on a summary application, and using that procedure did not make the ex parte decree a nullity. The dismissal of the tenant’s suit was correct.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 45-A and 45-B of the Banking Companies Act, 1949, as amended, gave the designated High Court jurisdiction over winding-up matters and full power to decide claims and related questions. Section 45-G empowered the High Court to make rules concerning procedure. In light of the Act’s purpose of expediting winding-up proceedings, the normal procedure under section 45-B, absent a contrary statutory provision or applicable rule, is a summary proceeding by application. The court may direct a suit, or rules may require one, having regard to the nature of the claim and the questions involved. The Court respectfully rejected the contrary approach in Sree Bank v. Mukherjee, [1950] 55 C.W.N. 400, but expressed no opinion on limitation.

predicates.bank_liquidation_claim: A claim is brought in the course of winding up a banking company.
predicates.claim_arises_in_winding_up: The claim concerns a matter that relates to or arises in the course of the winding up.
predicates.no_specific_procedure_requires_suit: No applicable law or court rule requires the particular claim to be pursued by a suit.

issues.definition: When a claim in a banking-company winding up arises from that winding up and no applicable rule requires a suit, the claim can be decided on a summary application.
